lever: Hidden composition of documented rules
mechanism: instruction.md documents 8-15 rules for a tool (e.g. a config merger or ledger reconciler) plus an explicit precedence/combination table; visible examples exercise each rule alone; hidden tests combine 2-4 rules and hit their error paths.
why_models_fail: Agents build locally correct per-rule handlers and test each rule in isolation; interactions and rejection paths are left unexercised.
qc_risk_note: Every combination outcome must follow from the written precedence table; include one worked combined example so the reviewer can trace each hidden case to text.
partial_credit_design: Tiers: single-rule cases 15%, pairwise combinations 35%, triple+ combinations 30%, documented error cases 20%; each tier is a weighted pytest group.
grader_cost: Low: oracle generates expected outputs; pytest compares.
not_copied_from: Inspired by SpecBench (036) visible-vs-held-out composition gap; differs: small offline CLI in a new domain, combination semantics written down, graded in tiers rather than as a gap metric.

lever: Audit-and-repair of a broken multi-stage pipeline against a documented contract
mechanism: Ship a 4-6 stage data or build pipeline with 5-8 independent defects of different kinds (logic, ordering, unit, concurrency, silent truncation). Only the end-to-end contract and per-stage contracts are documented, never the bug list.
why_models_fail: Agents fix the first visible failure and stop; downstream defects are masked by upstream ones; silent defects produce plausible output.
qc_risk_note: Grader must check documented contracts, not 'did you find bug #4'. Each defect must violate a written contract clause.
partial_credit_design: One weighted check per stage contract plus an end-to-end check; downstream checks run on oracle-fed inputs so one upstream miss does not zero everything.
grader_cost: Medium: per-stage fixtures produced by the oracle pipeline.
not_copied_from: Inspired by LHTB 2.0 audit-and-repair category (008) and TB2 unsolved system tasks (001); differs: new pipeline, defects mapped one-to-one to written contract clauses, stage-isolated grading.

lever: Algorithmic lift on a size ladder
mechanism: Provide a correct but naive reference program and the exact input sizes and time limit per size. Small and medium sizes pass with library-level speedups; the largest needs a reformulation (incremental update, different data structure, decomposition). Output must match the reference exactly.
why_models_fail: Models apply surface-level speedups (vectorise, Numba, better call) and anchor on the given structure; the needed reformulation is an insight.
qc_risk_note: Must be hard for the agent, not the computer: oracle must run the largest size in under ~10% of the limit on the stated hardware; state the hardware.
partial_credit_design: Weighted by size tier (e.g. 10/20/30/40%); correctness gate per tier; no credit for a tier that exceeds the limit.
grader_cost: Medium: timing on fixed hardware; repeat 3x and take the min to cut noise.
not_copied_from: Inspired by BenchEvolver 'dominant algorithmic lift' (010) and AlgoTune (015); differs: agentic terminal task with exact-match outputs and fixed size tiers instead of open-ended speedup.

lever: Stacked orthogonal artifact constraints
mechanism: Ask for one artifact (binary, package, container layer, dataset) that must meet 4-5 independent written constraints at once, e.g. reproducible byte-identical output, pinned versions, a size cap, a target platform, no network at runtime.
why_models_fail: Each extra constraint multiplies the dependent work; models drop or rationalise away the costliest one.
qc_risk_note: Each constraint must be essential to the scenario, not decoration; avoid more than 5.
partial_credit_design: One weighted check per constraint plus a functional check; artifact must work for any credit.
not_copied_from: Inspired by CompileBench one-constraint collapse (019); differs: not cross-compiling curl; the constraints are reproducibility and policy limits in a new artifact.

lever: Dependent multi-stage chain with no shortcut
mechanism: 8-12 stages where each stage needs the verified output of the previous one (e.g. recover a parameter from stage-1 data, which decodes stage-2 input, ...). All procedures are documented; no stage can be done out of order.
why_models_fail: Errors compound across dependent steps and an early wrong value poisons later steps; success falls with coherent length.
qc_risk_note: Each stage must be individually fair and documented; avoid puzzle-hunt style hidden hints.
partial_credit_design: Checkpoint file per stage; credit for each correct checkpoint, ordered (Cybench-style subtask ladder).
not_copied_from: Inspired by METR time-horizon results (011, 020) and Cybench subtasks (013); differs: deterministic engineering stages, not CTF flags.

lever: Format-only validator plus self-verification burden
mechanism: Provide a validator that the instruction states checks format only. Correctness criteria (invariants, totals, cross-file consistency) are written in the spec and must be checked by the agent itself.
why_models_fail: Agents treat a passing validator as done and submit unchecked (premature completion).
qc_risk_note: Must clearly say the validator is format-only; otherwise it is a gotcha.
partial_credit_design: Format 5%, each documented invariant a separate weighted check.
not_copied_from: Inspired by MLE-bench validation-server non-use (017) and LHTB false finishes (002); differs: deliberately partial validator, stated as partial.

lever: Mixed feasible and infeasible instances with certificates
mechanism: A batch of scheduling or allocation requests under written constraints; some are provably infeasible. Feasible ones need a valid (or optimal) plan; infeasible ones need a minimal conflicting subset as certificate.
why_models_fail: Models invent a plan for unsolvable instances and rarely prove infeasibility.
qc_risk_note: Certificate format and validity rule must be written; grader verifies the certificate, not a fixed answer.
partial_credit_design: Per instance: feasible plan valid 1 pt (optimal +0.5); infeasible flag 0.5, valid certificate +0.5.
not_copied_from: Inspired by PlanBench unsolvable-instance results (028); differs: terminal batch job with checkable infeasibility certificates.

lever: Documented quiet failure in a provided component
mechanism: A provided library or CLI has a man page that documents a behaviour on certain input classes (e.g. returns a sentinel, truncates at a limit). Inputs contain such cases; correct output requires handling them.
why_models_fail: Silent wrong outputs are propagated; agents do not read the full tool doc or check outputs.
qc_risk_note: Risk of being judged a gimmick ('technically correct but suggests the wrong answer', 005). Keep the behaviour natural for the domain and mention the doc in the instruction.
partial_credit_design: Normal cases 50%, quiet-failure cases 50%, weighted per case class.
not_copied_from: Inspired by PlanBench-XL implicit tool failures (030); differs: offline, documented behaviour, no tool ecosystem.

lever: Small set of interacting ad-hoc rules with precedence
mechanism: 15-30 non-commonsense rules (written, numbered) with an explicit precedence order, applied to a batch of cases via a stateful tool where some actions are single-use.
why_models_fail: Models fall back on common-sense priors over written ad-hoc rules and miss single-use/collect-first constraints.
qc_risk_note: Keep the rule count modest; TB reviewers reject hardness from many corner cases (005).
partial_credit_design: Per-case final-state comparison; weight cases by number of interacting rules.
not_copied_from: Inspired by tau-bench policy failures (014); differs: no simulated user, offline deterministic batch, precedence table given.

lever: Parameter identification within a documented model family
mechanism: The spec fully defines a parameterised family of behaviours; the agent observes outputs of an instance and must recover its parameters, then predict outputs on hidden scenarios.
why_models_fail: Requires designing experiments and generalising beyond the observed scenarios.
qc_risk_note: Family and identifiability must be documented; hidden scenarios must lie inside the documented family.
partial_credit_design: Parameter accuracy tiers plus hidden-scenario prediction accuracy.
not_copied_from: Inspired by LHTB 2.0 reconstruction tasks (008); differs: the model family is written down, removing the underspecification.

lever: Budget planning for a documented expensive job
mechanism: The stated time budget and hardware make the naive full recompute impossible; the agent must cache, reuse or compute incrementally.
why_models_fail: Agents ignore run-time cost and time out while busy.
qc_risk_note: Rubric criterion 'hard for the agent, not the computer' (006) and 'no resource pressure' (007). Only use with large oracle headroom and stated limits.
partial_credit_design: Fraction of required outputs produced within budget.
not_copied_from: Inspired by LHTB timeouts (002) and MLE-bench resource blindness (017).

lever: Misleading first hypothesis in a debugging task
mechanism: The first symptom suggests a common cause; later evidence (logs, a second test) contradicts it; the real cause is documented system behaviour.
why_models_fail: Stubborn early assumptions; ignoring contradictory information.
qc_risk_note: Must be a natural failure, not a planted trick; the docs must explain the real behaviour.
partial_credit_design: Root-cause fix check, regression check, no-collateral-damage check.
not_copied_from: Inspired by RE-Bench long-horizon agency failures (016).

lever: Optimality gap scoring on structured instances
mechanism: Large combinatorial instances with exploitable structure; generic ILP/brute force is too slow at the top size; score by gap to the oracle's optimum.
why_models_fail: Agents reach for generic solvers or greedy heuristics and miss the structure.
qc_risk_note: Oracle optimum must be provable; do not block package install (004 says disabling network is not a valid difficulty).
partial_credit_design: Valid solution 20%; then linear credit in gap from 10% down to 0%.
not_copied_from: Inspired by NPHardEval (029) and AlgoTune clamped scoring (015).

lever: Beat a fully documented fixed opponent or checker
mechanism: A deterministic opponent (bot, filter, compressor bound) with full source provided; the agent must produce a strategy that beats it on hidden seeds.
why_models_fail: Needs creative or adversarial reasoning and experimentation, not pattern-following.
qc_risk_note: Hidden seeds must come from a documented distribution.
partial_credit_design: Win-rate tiers (e.g. >50%, >70%, >90%).
not_copied_from: Inspired by TB2 human-medium/model-hard tasks (001); differs: new game or filter, not corewars or XSS.

lever: Novel fully specified formalism
mechanism: A new small DSL or VM with complete written semantics; the agent implements it and uses it to produce artifacts; hidden tests mix features and error cases.
why_models_fail: Lower prior familiarity; composition and error semantics.
qc_risk_note: Spec must be complete and unambiguous; give a reference grammar.
partial_credit_design: Feature tiers plus composition tier plus error tier.
not_copied_from: Inspired by PlanBench Mystery (028) and TB2 interpreter tasks (003 Table 3); differs: new formalism.

lever: Error-path and rejection weight
mechanism: Spec lists which inputs must be rejected and with which code; at least 25% of hidden weight is on invalid inputs.
why_models_fail: Agents optimise for the happy path; rejection is where a strong compiler still failed.
qc_risk_note: Every rejection rule written.
partial_credit_design: Separate weighted group for rejections.
not_copied_from: Inspired by SpecBench CCC error-detection failures (036).

lever: Spec-legal input variants in combination
mechanism: The input format spec allows several variants (quoting, encodings, line endings, optional fields); hidden inputs combine them.
why_models_fail: Agents test on the examples given and miss combined variants.
qc_risk_note: Risk of 'clerical difficulty' FAIL (006, 007). Keep as a minor weight only.
partial_credit_design: Small weight (<=15%) for variant combinations.
not_copied_from: Inspired by LHTB hidden stress cases (002); differs: all variants written in the spec.

lever: Coupled multi-module change in an original mid-size codebase
mechanism: An original 10-30k LOC codebase; the feature touches many modules with shared invariants.
why_models_fail: Success falls with files touched and engineering complexity.
qc_risk_note: High authoring cost; interfaces must be specified.
partial_credit_design: Per-module and integration tests weighted.
not_copied_from: Inspired by SWE-bench Pro file-count decline (012) and RE-Bench LOC R^2 (016).

lever: Stateful protocol with irreversible steps
mechanism: A local server with a documented protocol where some actions are irreversible and order matters; the agent must plan before acting.
why_models_fail: Agents act before collecting all needed information.
qc_risk_note: Server must be reset-safe for grading; the protocol must be fully documented.
partial_credit_design: Final server state per entity.
not_copied_from: Inspired by tau-bench single-use exchange failure (014).

lever: Interactive program driving as a secondary ingredient
mechanism: One stage requires operating a documented interactive program (REPL/TUI) where the state persists.
why_models_fail: Agents stall on interactive tools.
qc_risk_note: Weak evidence; harness tmux support must be checked.
partial_credit_design: Stage checkpoint.
not_copied_from: Inspired by TB discussion #224 (007).
